deities: Lord Ganesha (Tekdi Ganpati; self-manifested / Swayambhu idol, believed to be growing in size)
festivals: Tekdi Ganapati Yatra (grand yatra on Paush-month Sankashti Chaturthi)

history.dynasty: None documented; managed by the Tekdi Ganesh Mandir Samiti
history.period: Shrine tradition ~250 years old (per temple trust/local tradition; CONFLICT - see below); present structure 1978-1984
history.summary: The Shri Ganesh Tekdi Mandir, popularly called Tekdicha Ganpati (Ganpati of the hillock), stands atop a hillock on Station Road at Sitabuldi, next to Nagpur Railway Station. The Ganesh idol is worshipped as Swayambhu (self-manifested), believed by devotees to be growing in size over time, and the shrine is regarded as a Jagruta Devasthan (a living, awake deity). Local tradition claims the shrine is about 250 years old (some sources say 300 years or '210 years in business' per a listing), though legend also traces it to Hemandri Pandit - none of the antiquity claims is reliably documented (CONFLICT/verify). Documented modern history: after adjoining land was acquired in 1965, temple construction began in 1978 under devotee Ganpatrao Joshi and was completed in 1984, with the Defence Ministry granting an additional 20,000 sq ft since the hillock land belonged to the Military Defence wing; aarti is performed thrice daily and Modaka distributed. In 2024 the Maharashtra government elevated the temple from a Grade C to a Grade A tourism site, making it eligible for central funds under a Rs. 170-crore beautification plan.

name: Shri Ganesh Tekdi Mandir (Tekdicha Ganpati)
town_description: Nagpur is the winter capital and second capital of Maharashtra, the largest city of the Vidarbha region, and one of India's major commercial centres, famous for its oranges (the 'Orange City'). It is a premier rail junction connecting all four metropolitan cities, and is served by the Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar International Airport. Sitabuldi, at the city centre next to the railway station, holds the historic Sitabuldi Fort (site of the 1817 battle) and the hillock of the Tekdi Ganesh temple.

travel.airport: Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar International Airport, Nagpur; approx. 8 km by road via taxis and app cabs (per Justdial listing).
travel.railway: Nagpur Railway Station (Nagpur Junction) is a short walk from the temple (approx. 1 km or less), just east of the hillock.
travel.road: Station Road, Sitabuldi - central Nagpur; easily reached by auto-rickshaw, taxi or city bus; comfortable footwear recommended for the hillock climb.

visitor_information.best_time: October to February for pleasant weather. Ganesh Chaturthi and the Paush-month Tekdi Ganapati Yatra are the grandest but most crowded times; early mornings or sunset offer calmer darshan.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:30 AM to 9:00 PM daily (per the temple trust's own listing; one travel source mentions 6:00 AM to midnight - CONFLICT/verify).
